opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
“What can I do with you, Ephraim?
 What can I do with you, Judah?”

This line comes from the prophet Book of Hosea, specifically Hosea 6:4.

“What shall I do with you, Ephraim?
 What shall I do with you, Judah?
 Your love is like a morning cloud,
 like the dew that goes away early.”

The names here carry meaning. The Tribe of Ephraim had become the leading tribe of the northern kingdom of Israel, and the prophets often used its name to refer to the whole northern nation. The Kingdom of Judah was the southern kingdom. By naming both Ephraim and Judah, the prophet is speaking to the whole people of Israel.
God is lamenting their unsteady faithfulness. Their love appears for a moment but does not last, like the morning dew. It forms early and looks real, but once the sun rises, it quickly disappears.
This had become a pattern in Israel’s history. They would return to God for a time, make promises, perform the rituals of their faith, and then drift away again.
A few verses later, the prophet explains what God truly desires:
“For I desire mercy, not sacrifice,
 and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.” — Hosea 6:6
The problem Hosea describes has not disappeared. The idols today may not be made of wood or stone, but they still exist—control, security, success, and the things we trust instead of God.
Yet the message of Hosea is not only correction. God keeps calling His people back.
For those who have fallen away from the Church for whatever reason, the invitation is still the same: come back.
God wants to receive you. He wants to love you.
God already knows you.
Now He is calling you to know Him.
There is no coincidence that you are reading this today. This may be the invitation meant just for you. You do not have to dress up.
Come as you are—just return.
